label: SYNTHETIC READERS: a test instrument, never readers. Not a choice: the editor chooses (book.json Q3).
candidates_from: chapter-plan/study-name-and-structure.md, section The name (the storyteller's N1 to N6), at dev d24e984
method: title and subtitle alone, as on a shelf or a listing; no cover, no page; each persona answers which it would pick up, what each makes it expect, which it would buy, and why in one line

personas.why: Brakes is a word my risk committee already uses; every other title starts with a word I would have to look up.

expects.N1: a technical manual; 'agentic' tells me it is not for me
expects.N2: a book about staff, or about AI staff; not sure which
expects.N5: a book for engineers about infrastructure
expects.N6: how to let a company use AI quickly without losing control of it

personas.note: Picks up only N6. 'Agentic' in the title is jargon to this reader; in N6 it sits in the subtitle, where it does not block the first read.

personas.why: The brakes are the controls; a title that says the controls make you faster is the argument I need for my board.

expects.N1: a practitioner's how-to, credible because 'shown working'
expects.N2: an organisational book about AI teams
expects.N3: an engineering design book; 'provenance' is the word that caught me
expects.N4: 'open' worries me before I know what it means: open to whom?
expects.N5: non-functional requirements, so engineering; I would pass it to my architects
expects.N6: controls as an enabler, with evidence from a real record

personas.note: Would also pick up N1 for the word 'shown'. N4's 'open' reads as exposure to a security reader until the subtitle explains it.

personas.why: 'Shown working' says there is a real system behind it, and 'how to build yours' says I get something to copy.

expects.N1: a worked example of agentic workflows, end to end, with the method to reuse
expects.N2: a walkthrough, close to N1 but about the team rather than the workflow
expects.N3: a design book on coordination between agents
expects.N5: the engineering underneath, honest but narrow
expects.N6: a management book with a good line

personas.note: N2 a close second. Finds N6 memorable but expects less substance from it.

personas.why: Protocols, provenance and memory are the three things I fight with every day; the subtitle tells me exactly what is inside.

expects.N1: a case study; would check whether the code is real
expects.N2: a walkthrough for leads more than builders
expects.N3: concrete engineering: how agents share state and record what they did
expects.N5: an honest engineer's title; would read it
expects.N6: a talk turned into a book; fun, probably light

personas.note: N5 a close second. The only persona for whom a 'plain words' title (N3) beats a hook.

personas.why: It is the only one that sounds like a book rather than a course; four titles start with the same word as the rest of the shelf.

expects.N1: another title in the agentic row
expects.N2: clean and short; I could set it big on a cover
expects.N5: a strong image, plumbing, but a narrow promise
expects.N6: a story with an argument, and a phrase people will repeat

personas.note: Notes 'So We Can' is long for a cover line, and that N2 is the best typographic title of the six.

personas.why: The team is what I manage; 'from an empty repository to a talk on stage' is a project from start to finish, and I want to see how it was run.

expects.N2: how a team of agents was organised and run, start to finish
expects.N4: keeping a team aligned: 'aligned' is the word that pulled me
expects.N6: a book about going faster safely; would look inside

personas.note: N4 a second for 'aligned'. The only persona to pick N2 first.

personas.why: It reads like a headline, and it is a claim I can test against the record; 'in a day' in N1's subtitle is the better story hook.

expects.N1: a team of agents built a talk in a day: that is the story
expects.N6: a counter-intuitive claim about speed and control

personas.note: Would pick up N6 and N1. Warns that N6 promises a causal claim ('so we can go faster') the book must earn.

personas.why: 'How to build yours' is the promise I buy books for; the rest describe something someone else did.

expects.N1: a worked example and a playbook for my own team
expects.N6: a great talk title; would watch the talk, not sure I would buy the book

personas.note: N6 a second. Only N1's subtitle promises something the reader can do.
